answer: Sybil resistance derives from making each identity complete a chain of sequential modular squarings, where every result depends on the preceding one. GPUs can process separate clones in parallel, but cannot collapse the work or shorten an individual chain; multiplying identities therefore requires multiplying resources and waiting through each chain’s delay. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently, while trellis, sparrow, and nectar serve only as labels, not shortcuts.
